title: DNS over HTTPS causes long buffering in YouTube
body: I'm using Firefox 127 on Windows 10. If I set DNS over HTTPS to Max Protection with Cloudflare and hard-refresh a YouTube video, loading is consistently delayed by at least 10 seconds and sometimes by 30 seconds or more. The video may also freeze around the 20-second mark. The Network Monitor shows many NS_BINDING_ABORTED entries for videoplayback requests that are absent when DNS over HTTPS is disabled. With DNS over HTTPS completely disabled, videos load nearly instantly and do not pause. Max Protection is the only setting that reproduces the delay consistently. I attached a screenshot of the Network Monitor.

symptoms_visible: With DNS over HTTPS set to Max Protection using Cloudflare, hard-refreshing a YouTube video takes at least 10 seconds and sometimes more than 30 seconds to start.
The video sometimes freezes around the 20-second mark, and the Network Monitor shows many NS_BINDING_ABORTED videoplayback requests.
With DNS over HTTPS disabled, the same videos load nearly instantly and do not pause.
N0.label: N0 YouTube buffering with Max Protection reported

symptoms_visible: I can reproduce the long YouTube delay in a new profile where the only change is Max Protection with Cloudflare, and I can reproduce it on my laptop too.
I cannot reproduce it in a Windows sandbox, even after installing the extensions I normally suspected.
N1.label: N1 clean-profile reproduction and network log collected

symptoms_visible: My ISP does not support IPv6, and the delay reproduces on IPv4-only connections.
When I use a phone connection that supports IPv6, YouTube works with Max Protection.
The buffering has also been seen with secure DNS providers other than Cloudflare.
N2.label: N2 behavior correlated with lack of IPv6

symptoms_visible: In a new Firefox 127.0.1 profile, enabling network.http.http3.retry_different_ip_family makes Max Protection fail less often, but loading succeeds only about half the time.
N3.label: N3 alternate-IP-family preference only partially improves behavior

symptoms_visible: The provided test build loaded YouTube flawlessly through a couple dozen hard refreshes without a single failure.
The regular Firefox 127.0.1 profile still succeeds only about half the time with the alternate-IP-family preference enabled.
N4.label: N4 candidate test build verified

symptoms_visible: The provided test build loaded YouTube flawlessly with Max Protection through a couple dozen hard refreshes.
A maintainer reports that the fallback-connection correction has landed; I have not reported a retest of the landed Firefox build.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix landed after candidate-build verification

question_patterns: Can you reproduce the delay in a new profile created through about:profiles?
Does it happen on another machine or in a clean Windows environment?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can reproduce it consistently in a new profile, and the only setting I changed was DNS over HTTPS to Max Protection with Cloudflare. I can reproduce it on my laptop too. I could not reproduce it in a Windows sandbox, even after installing uBlock Origin and Privacy Badger there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It does not reproduce in a new profile; it only happens in my existing profile and stops when I disable one extension.
It reproduces in the new profile and on my desktop, but I have not tested a second physical machine.

question_patterns: Can you capture an HTTP log from about:logging while reproducing the delay and send the downloaded file?
Please record an about:logging trace during a delayed YouTube load and share the raw file.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I captured the network log while reproducing the problem and sent it to the corrected email address.

edges.comment: Comments c2-c5, reporter's systems: the reporter reproduced in a clean profile and on a laptop, did not reproduce in Windows Sandbox, and sent the requested raw network log after receiving the corrected address.

question_patterns: Does your ISP provide IPv6, and can you compare the behavior on a connection that supports IPv6?
Is the delay limited to networks without IPv6 connectivity?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My ISP does not support IPv6 either. I reproduced the problem through two ISPs without IPv6, while connecting through my phone on an IPv6-capable mobile carrier made YouTube work with Max Protection.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My connection has working IPv6, and the same delay occurs over both IPv4 and IPv6.
My ISP has no IPv6 and the issue reproduces there, but I cannot test an IPv6-capable connection.

edges.comment: Comments c6-c8: the reporter confirmed their ISP lacks IPv6; another affected user supplied the two-ISP and IPv6-capable mobile comparison, and other affected users reported similar buffering with Cloudflare, NextDNS, or Quad9. These affected users are folded into one simulated user side without importing unrelated symptoms.

question_patterns: In a new profile, enable network.http.http3.retry_different_ip_family and tell me how often the problem still occurs.
Could you toggle network.http.http3.retry_different_ip_family in about:config and repeat several hard refreshes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I enabled it in a new profile using Firefox 127.0.1. Max Protection seemed to fail less frequently, but it was still only about a 50% success rate.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After enabling the preference, every hard refresh loads immediately and I cannot reproduce the buffering at all.
It improves the success rate from almost never to roughly 60%, but delayed loads still occur regularly.

edges.comment: Comments c10-c12, reporter's Firefox 127.0.1 test profile: this handler-requested about:config probe is modeled as a measurement. The reporter supplies only the observed partial improvement, not a conclusion about the networking mechanism.

question_patterns: Could you run this test build and repeatedly hard-refresh YouTube with Max Protection enabled?
Please test the provided build against the same videos and report whether the delay still occurs.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried the build, and it worked flawlessly. I hard-refreshed a couple dozen times and it did not fail a single time.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The provided build still has the same 10-to-30-second delay on most hard refreshes.
The provided build passed ten hard refreshes instead of a couple dozen, with no delayed starts.

question_patterns: Can you capture another HTTP log while the regular build still shows intermittent failures?
Please share the raw about:logging output from the remaining failures in the new profile.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I uploaded two logs from the remaining behavior and shared the link. The link expires in seven days.

edges.comment: Comments c9-c15, reporter's machine: the reporter tested the provided pre-landing build and separately shared two raw network logs after the preference probe. Both are measurement clarifications; the log's causal interpretation remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Correct the HTTP/3 fallback-connection success handling so that a usable fallback is accepted when the speculative transaction closes with NS_OK, then ship that networking fix and ask the reporter to verify it in a build containing the landed change.
solution.concrete_example: The network log shows an HTTP/3 connection trying an unreachable address family, followed by a fallback connection that is created but not accepted because SpeculativeTransaction recognizes only NS_BASE_STREAM_CLOSED as success while this connection closes with NS_OK. Extend the success check to accept that close reason, ship the correction, and ask the reporter to retest today's build with Max Protection enabled.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied raw network logs and observed that the candidate build worked. The maintainer inferred from the log that Firefox first attempted an HTTP/3 connection over unsupported IPv6, started a fallback, and then rejected the usable fallback because SpeculativeTransaction treated NS_BASE_STREAM_CLOSED but not NS_OK as success. Naming that mechanism is engineer inference, not user-provided evidence.

edges.comment: Comments c13-c16 and c18-c29: the maintainer's final accepted diagnosis was the fallback connection being disregarded because of its close reason, and the patch added the corresponding success check. The reporter verified the candidate test build in c11, but did not later report testing a regular landed build; uplift, backout/reland logistics, and release scheduling are intentionally not scored.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: on a connection without IPv6, the attempted HTTP/3 connection cannot be established, and Firefox starts but fails to accept a usable fallback because SpeculativeTransaction does not recognize the NS_OK close reason as success.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the clean-profile reproduction, the IPv4-only versus IPv6-capable network comparison, and the collected network logs rather than inferred from YouTube buffering alone.
Must fix the fallback-connection success handling so the usable fallback is accepted; disabling DNS over HTTPS may avoid the symptom but is not the technical resolution.
Must not treat network.http.http3.retry_different_ip_family as a complete fix, because the reporter still observed failures in roughly half of the tests with it enabled.

Must use the flawless provided-build test as pre-landing verification and ask the reporter to retest a build containing the landed fix; because no such post-landing reporter result appears in the thread, must not claim the reporter confirmed the shipped build.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical Firefox user who can create clean profiles, change DNS-over-HTTPS and about:config settings, capture network logs, test builds, and compare behavior across physical and sandboxed systems.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and concise, with concrete reproduction rates and environment comparisons; follows diagnostic instructions closely and asks whether additional logs are needed.
